outcome: CAP-03.S06 now provides one versioned fourteen-profile workflow catalog; profile-specific Research Intent defaults and explicit researcher acceptance; history-preserving profile revision and migration; durable primary-stage, supporting-handoff, checkpoint, completion, revisit, stale-impact, restart and compare-and-swap authority; and an accessible adaptive desktop path whose production frame preserves all implemented tools while guiding the selected scholarly workflow.

environmentNotes: Two initial pnpm launches resolved host Node 20 instead of the repository toolchain; one contract run nevertheless passed and the desktop run stopped before discovery on its declared engine requirement. The authoritative desktop and contract replays put the repository-pinned Node 24.19.0 runtime first on PATH and passed completely.

The first desktop performance run passed all workflow-facing metrics but one unrelated accessible-table p95 sample exceeded its committed regression threshold by 1.796 ms. The complete unchanged replay passed every metric, including that table at 43.198 ms versus the 46.916 ms threshold; the first sample is retained as transient measurement variance, not hidden or used as passing evidence.

The project-lifecycle performance tool refuses any tracked or untracked file even with --measure-only. The only worktree dirt is the protected pre-existing W1.A04.B00 witness, which this campaign must not read, hash, stage, delete or move. That cross-capability benchmark and storage-maintenance performance remain explicitly gate-bound to clean-clone W1-exit qualification; navigation/render performance is directly qualified here.
The protected pre-existing untracked W1.A04.B00 witness remained untouched and unstaged throughout slice verification.
